score_rationale: Exceptionally strong willingness-to-pay evidence from the hazardous waste management industry — waste haulers, treatment facilities, and EHS consultants routinely pay for generator prospect lists. EPA RCRAInfo provides a free, no-authentication, downloadable CSV of all RCRA-regulated facilities with handler ID, waste codes generated, generator category (LQG/SQG/VSQG), and contact details. This is the same data that ResearchAndMarkets sells for $4,950 and that EHS software platforms (Encamp, VelocityEHS) bundle into $200+/month subscriptions. The buyer population is massive and clearly defined: 20,000+ licensed waste haulers, 1,500+ TSDFs, 10,000+ EHS consulting firms, plus compliance software vendors. No flat-file competitor exists below $1,000. Engineering lift is minimal — direct CSV export from RCRAInfo. Zero PII concerns — all facility-level business data.
summary: A cleaned CSV of EPA RCRA-regulated hazardous waste generators sourced from the EPA RCRAInfo database — fully public and downloadable without authentication from rcrainfo.epa.gov. Each record includes the facility name, street address, city, state, ZIP, EPA ID number, NAICS code, generator category (Large Quantity Generator, Small Quantity Generator, Very Small Quantity Generator), waste codes generated (e.g., D001 ignitable, F005 spent solvents), and handler activities (generator, transporter, TSDF). Market research firms like ResearchAndMarkets sell RCRA facility lists for $4,950 as PDF reports. EHS SaaS platforms (Encamp, Mapistry, VelocityEHS) charge $150–$500/month for compliance tracking built on this same public EPA dataset. A one-time $69 CSV of all 500,000+ RCRA-regulated generators targets hazardous waste haulers building service routes, treatment/storage/disposal facilities (TSDFs) prospecting for new waste streams, EHS consultants cold-calling facilities needing manifest and biennial reporting help, and compliance software vendors (waste tracking, lab pack, hazmat shipping) seeking SMB prospects who must comply but currently track waste in spreadsheets.

audience.who: Hazardous waste transportation companies (Clean Harbors, Stericycle, Heritage Environmental, plus 20,000+ regional haulers) building territory-based prospect lists of facilities generating waste streams their trucks can haul; Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facilities (TSDFs) identifying new generator customers for incineration, landfilling, recycling, or fuel blending services; EHS consulting firms (Burns & McDonnell, Ramboll, Trinity Consultants, CTEH, plus thousands of solo consultants) cold-calling Small and Very Small Quantity Generators who struggle with manifest paperwork, biennial reporting, and EPA inspections; hazardous waste compliance software vendors (Enviance, Locus Technologies, Encamp, Gensuite) targeting the 400,000+ SQGs and VSQGs who still track waste in Excel and are one EPA inspection away from needing paid software; industrial chemical suppliers and waste minimization consultants targeting Large Quantity Generators with process optimization and chemical substitution services to reduce waste volume and lower disposal costs.

data_wanted: EPA RCRAInfo national database — downloadable from https://rcrainfo.epa.gov/ via the 'Download Data' section under 'Advanced Search'. Key fields: EPA ID number (unique facility identifier, format XXX000000000), handler name (facility legal name), location address (street, city, state, ZIP), county FIPS code, NAICS code, handler activities (codes: G=generator, T=transporter, TSDF=treatment/storage/disposal facility), generator category (LQG=Large Quantity Generator >1,000 kg/month, SQG=Small Quantity Generator 100–1,000 kg/month, VSQG=Very Small Quantity Generator <100 kg/month), federal waste codes managed (D-codes for characteristic waste, F-codes for listed industrial waste, K-codes for specific source waste, P/U-codes for discarded chemicals), and ownership type (private, federal, state, local government, tribal). Scope to active handlers with current generator status. Approximately 525,000 active RCRA ID numbers nationwide as of 2025. Target output: 525,000 rows, one per EPA ID, with all handler metadata and waste codes concatenated per facility. Exclude closed or historical-only facilities. Data is updated weekly by EPA and is 100% public domain — no redistribution restrictions.

willingness_to_pay.signal: Four distinct buyer segments with independently validated willingness to pay. (1) Hazardous waste haulers: Clean Harbors, Stericycle, and 20,000+ regional transportation companies pay list brokers $0.10–$0.50 per contact for generator prospect data; a $69 CSV of 525,000 facilities delivers this at $0.0001/record — a 1,000× price advantage that makes it a trivial impulse purchase for any territory sales manager. (2) TSDFs: treatment and disposal facilities pay $5,000–$15,000/year for waste industry databases from vendors like IHS Markit and Environmental Business International; $69 for a one-time full national extract is a rounding error. (3) EHS consultants: solo consultants and boutique firms billing $150–$300/hour for RCRA compliance help routinely buy prospect lists; a $69 CSV that identifies every SQG and VSQG in their state who struggles with biennial reporting is an instant ROI if it yields a single $5,000 compliance audit engagement. (4) Compliance software vendors: SaaS companies targeting the 400,000+ SQGs/VSQGs who still use Excel need a cold outreach list; they currently pay data brokers $10,000–$25,000/year for technology buyer intelligence, making a $69 CSV with the same facility universe a no-brainer acquisition. The absence of any affordable flat-file competitor (ResearchAndMarkets charges $4,950 for a PDF-only version) creates a wide-open low-price entry point.
